question: The image formed by a concave lens for an object at infinity is:
solution:
The correct answer is __**virtual, erect, and point-sized**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **concave lens** is also known as a **diverging lens** because it diverges the light rays that pass through it parallel to its **principal axis**.
 
• When an **object is placed at infinity**, the incident rays are parallel to the **principal axis**. After **refraction** through the concave lens, these rays appear to diverge from the **principal focus (F1)** located on the same side as the object.
 
• The image formed under these conditions is **virtual**, meaning it cannot be obtained on a screen, and it is **erect** (upright).
 
• In terms of size, the image is **highly diminished** or **point-sized** at the **focus**.
 
• This behavior is consistent regardless of the **focal length** of the concave lens, as its primary function is to spread out light rays.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Image Formation for Other Positions:** Unlike convex lenses, a **concave lens** always produces a **virtual, erect, and diminished** image, regardless of the **object's distance** from the lens. If the object is moved from **infinity** closer to the **optical center**, the image moves from the **focus** toward the **optical center** and increases slightly in size, but remains smaller than the object.
 
• **Lens Formula and Magnification:** The relationship between object distance (u), image distance (v), and focal length (f) is given by **1/f = 1/v - 1/u**. For a concave lens, the **magnification (m = v/u)** is always **positive** and **less than 1**, confirming the image is always **erect** and **diminished**.
 
• **Sign Convention:** According to the **Cartesian sign convention**, the **focal length** of a **concave lens** is always taken as **negative**. Similarly, the **image distance (v)** is also **negative** because the virtual image is formed on the left side of the lens (the same side as the object).
 
• **Practical Applications:** Concave lenses are widely used in **spectacles** to correct **Myopia** (nearsightedness), in **peepholes** of house doors to provide a wide view of people outside, and in **flashlights** to spread the light beam over a larger area.
 
• **Power of Lens:** The **power** of a concave lens is expressed in **Dioptres (D)** and is always **negative**, calculated as the reciprocal of the focal length in meters (**P = 1/f**).
